collections.name: Museo Gregoriano Egizio
collections.description: Founded 1839 by Gregory XVI, this museum houses one of the world's most important collections of Egyptian antiquities outside Cairo. Most objects were already in Rome since antiquity — from the Gardens of Sallust, Hadrian's Villa at Tivoli, and Roman Egypt. Nine rooms plus a hemicycle and Terrace of the Niche.

artworks.title: Ramesses II Enthroned
artworks.description: Fragmented statue of the great pharaoh Ramesses II seated on a throne, from Room I's epigraphic collection.

artworks.title: Mummy with Yellow Coffin
artworks.description: Among the oldest wood paintings in history — the famous 'yellow coffins' of the Third Intermediate Period with intricate funerary iconography.

artworks.title: Osiris-Antinous
artworks.description: Statue of Antinous, Hadrian's beloved, depicted as the god Osiris. Found at Hadrian's Villa, Tivoli.

artworks.title: Eight Sekhmet Statues
artworks.description: Eight statues of the lioness goddess Sekhmet from the Temple Precinct of Mut at Karnak, plus four more in the hemicycle. Part of Amenhotep III's funerary temple, Thebes.

artworks.title: Statue of Queen Tuya
artworks.description: Statue of Queen Tuya, mother of Ramesses II, from the Gardens of Sallust collection.

artworks.title: Colossal Statue of the Nile
artworks.description: Reclining river-god of the Nile with crocodile at his feet, a Roman interpretation of the Egyptian river deity.

artworks.title: Bronze Pinecone
artworks.description: Colossal Roman bronze pinecone, nearly 4 meters high. Originally a fountain near the Pantheon, later in the atrium of Old St. Peter's — cited by Dante (Inferno XXXI). Moved to the Cortile della Pigna in 1608.

artworks.title: Book of the Dead
artworks.description: The famous Egyptian funerary text — spells and formulas to guide the deceased through the afterlife.

artworks.title: Lions of Nectanebo
artworks.description: Two reclining lion statues flanking the fountain, from the reign of Nectanebo II, Dynasty XXX.

artworks.title: Naophorus of Udjahorresnet
artworks.description: Statue of Udjahorresnet carrying a naos shrine — the most important historical document in the collection, from the Persian conquest period.

artworks.title: Sarcophagus of Djedmut
artworks.description: Sarcophagus of Djedmut, singer of Amon-Ra at Karnak, early Dynasty XXII.

artworks.title: Shroud of the Lady of the Vatican
artworks.description: Roman-era linen shroud from Antinopolis, preserved with its painted decoration intact.

collections.name: Museo Chiaramonti
collections.description: Founded by Pius VII Chiaramonti in the early 19th century. A long loggia of approximately 1,000 sculptures — one of the most important collections of Roman portrait busts in the world. Arranged by Antonio Canova after the Napoleonic looting and the 1815 recovery.

artworks.title: Gallery of 1,000 Roman Busts
artworks.description: Approximately 1,000 Roman portrait busts lining both walls of the 300m loggia — emperors, emperors' wives, philosophers, orators. A 'gallery of famous names from antiquity.'

artworks.title: Heracles with Infant Telephos
artworks.description: Roman copy of a Greek original showing Hercules with his infant son Telephos.

artworks.title: Red Marble Papal Throne
artworks.description: The red marble papal throne formerly in the Basilica of St. John Lateran.

artworks.title: Canova's Fresco Cycle
artworks.description: Frescoes commemorating papal patronage and the return of Vatican works from France after the Napoleonic looting.

collections.name: Braccio Nuovo (New Wing)
collections.description: A 68-meter neoclassical gallery built by Raffaele Stern in the early 19th century. Houses some of the Vatican's greatest Roman statues, including the Augustus of Prima Porta.

artworks.title: Augustus of Prima Porta
artworks.description: The most famous portrait type of Emperor Augustus. Found 1863 at the Villa of Livia. Augustus in military dress (adlocutio pose), cuirass decorated with allegorical reliefs including the Parthian returning standards. Based on Polykleitos' Doryphoros pose.

artworks.title: Roman Copy of the Doryphoros (Spear-Bearer)
artworks.description: Roman marble copy of Polykleitos' canonical 5th-century BCE Greek bronze, the ultimate classical statement of male proportion and contrapposto.

artworks.title: Statue of the Nile
artworks.description: Roman river-god reclining with the Nile's tributaries; crocodile at his feet.

artworks.title: Gilded Bronze Peacocks
artworks.description: Two splendid gilt-bronze peacocks; originals from Hadrian's tomb (Castel Sant'Angelo). The Cortile della Pigna peacocks are copies of these.

collections.name: Museo Pio-Clementino
collections.description: Founded 1771 by Clement XIV, enlarged by Pius VI. The first public museum of antiquity in the modern sense. 12 rooms and galleries housing the Vatican's greatest collection of classical sculpture.

artworks.title: Laocoon and His Sons
artworks.description: Trojan priest Laocoon and his sons strangled by sea serpents after he warned against the Trojan Horse. Discovered on the Esquiline Hill in 1506; purchased by Julius II. Pliny called it 'superior to all other works of painting and sculpture.' The defining masterpiece of Hellenistic pathos and anatomy.

artworks.title: Apollo Belvedere
artworks.date: c. 120–140 CE (copy of 4th c. BCE Greek original)
artworks.description: The god after shooting his arrow, in a pose of ideal grace and contrapposto. The benchmark of classical male beauty for 500 years; endlessly copied and quoted by Canova, Thorvaldsen, and many others.

artworks.title: Belvedere Torso
artworks.date: 1st century BCE (copy of early 2nd c. BCE bronze)
artworks.description: A powerfully seated male nude, muscles twisted in a spiral. Now identified as Ajax the Lesser contemplating suicide. Michelangelo revered it above all antiquities and used it as the model for many Sistine Chapel figures.

artworks.title: Perseus Triumphant
artworks.description: Perseus holds the severed head of Medusa, standing in graceful contrapposto. Canova's masterpiece created after the Napoleonic looting; symbol of the restored collection.

artworks.title: Sleeping Ariadne
artworks.artist: Unknown (Roman copy of 2nd c. BCE original)
artworks.description: Ariadne abandoned on Naxos, discovered in the 16th century and long mistaken for Cleopatra. A favorite of Renaissance and Baroque artists for her pose of vulnerable sleep.

artworks.title: Gilded Bronze Hercules
artworks.description: Colossal bronze statue of Hercules, found near the Theatre of Pompey; a rare surviving monumental ancient bronze.

artworks.title: Braschi Antinous
artworks.description: Over-life-size marble bust of Antinous, Hadrian's beloved, found at Palestrina; one of the finest Antinous portraits in existence.

artworks.title: Porphyry Sarcophagus of St. Helena
artworks.description: Sarcophagus of Helena, mother of Constantine, made of imperial porphyry — the red Egyptian stone reserved for the imperial family.

artworks.title: Porphyry Sarcophagus of Constance
artworks.description: Sarcophagus of Constantina (Constance), daughter of Constantine, in imperial porphyry.

artworks.title: The Three Graces
artworks.description: A version of the famous Three Graces group, displayed along the walls of the Cabinet of the Masks.

artworks.title: Apoxyomenos (The Scraper)
artworks.description: Roman copy of Lysippus' famous athlete scraping oil from his body with a strigil — a canonical classical pose.

artworks.title: Barberini Candelabra
artworks.description: Ancient marble candelabrum from the Barberini collection.

artworks.title: Biga (Ancient Chariot)
artworks.description: Ancient two-horse chariot sculpture displayed in the Octagonal Court area.

artworks.title: Sarcophagus of Scipio Barbatus
artworks.description: Epitaph of Lucius Cornelius Scipio Barbatus — an important early Latin inscription on a sarcophagus.

artworks.title: Divinita Fluviale (Arno)
artworks.description: Reclining river-god figure representing the Arno river.

collections.name: Museo Gregoriano Etrusco
collections.description: Founded by Gregory XVI, inaugurated 2 February 1837 — one of the first museums dedicated to Etruscan antiquities. 22 rooms in the Palazzetto del Belvedere. Approximately 15,000 inventoried works, 4,000 on display.

artworks.title: Regolini-Galassi Tomb Assemblage
artworks.description: Tomb discovered intact in 1836 at Cerveteri — the richest Etruscan tomb ever found. Jewels including a spectacular pectoral, large fibula, bracelets, necklace; silver vessels including oinochoe, hemispherical cup, patera, skyphos, amphora; bronze funerary bed; three restored carts; shields.

artworks.title: Mars of Todi
artworks.description: A masterpiece of Etruscan bronze work — a statuette of a warrior (Mars) with a helmet, originally holding a shield and spear. Found in Todi in 1835.

artworks.title: Exekias Amphora
artworks.description: Signed by Exekias, the greatest Attic black-figure vase painter — depicts Achilles and Ajax playing a board game. A history of ancient Greek painting from Etruscan graves.

artworks.title: Etruscan Gold Jewelry Collection
artworks.description: Refined gold pieces from Cerveteri and Tarquinia demonstrating Etruscan goldwork mastery at its peak.

artworks.title: Funerary Monument with Dying Adonis
artworks.description: Important Etruscan funerary art depicting the dying Adonis.

artworks.title: Attic Kylix Attributed to Douris
artworks.description: Kylix attributed to Douris depicting Jason — from the Etruscan vase collection.

artworks.title: Cinerary Urn of the Master of Oenomaus
artworks.description: Cinerary urn by the Etruscan artist known as the Master of Oenomaus.

collections.name: Galleria dei Candelabri
collections.description: An approximately 80-meter corridor with six sections divided by pairs of massive ancient marble candelabra. Built as an open loggia in 1761 by Pius VI; completely renovated under Leo XIII (1883–1887) with frescoes by Ludwig Seitz.

artworks.title: Gigantic Toe of a Right Foot
artworks.description: Colossal toe from a statue approximately 13 meters tall, found near the Colosseum — possibly from the Temple of Venus and Rome.

artworks.title: Artemis of Ephesus
artworks.description: Fertility goddess Artemis of Ephesus, depicted with multiple breasts/bull testicles — a striking ancient icon of abundance.

artworks.title: Hypnos (God of Sleep) and Thanatos (Genius of Death)
artworks.description: Two statues from the Villa of Cassius, Tivoli (found 1774) — personifications of Sleep and Death, after Praxiteles.

artworks.title: Statue of an Old Fisherman
artworks.description: Striking realistic portrait of an old fisherman, from Anzio (found 1773) — remarkable for its unidealized naturalism.

artworks.title: Boy Strangling a Goose
artworks.description: Copy after Boethus — a playful genre scene of a boy strangling a goose, from the Villa Quintili (found 1789).

artworks.title: The Persian Warrior
artworks.description: Roman copy of a votive group of Attalos II of Pergamon — a dying Persian warrior. Found 1503–1512 at Palazzo Medici/Madama.

artworks.title: Ludwig Seitz Ceiling Frescoes
artworks.description: Grand ceiling series honoring St. Thomas Aquinas, painted by Ludwig Seitz under Leo XIII. Also frescoes by Domenico Torti (The Triumph of Truth).

artworks.title: Dionysus on a Satyr
artworks.description: Dionysus standing on a satyr — a playful Dionysiac group.

artworks.title: Circular Altar
artworks.description: Circular altar with a sacrifice scene featuring Mercury, from Tor Colombaro on the Appian Way.

collections.name: Galleria degli Arazzi
collections.description: A 75-meter corridor displaying magnificent tapestries. The left wall features Raphael tapestries designed by Raphael and woven in Brussels for the Sistine Chapel; the right wall displays ancient pontifical tapestries.

artworks.title: Raphael Tapestries
artworks.medium: Wool, silk, gold and silver thread
artworks.description: Designed by Raphael and woven in Brussels by Pieter van Aelst's workshop for the Sistine Chapel, commissioned by Clement VII. The cartoons were drawn bottom-to-top for low-warp looms. Subjects include Christ's charge to Peter, the stoning of St. Stephen, the conversion of St. Paul, and more. The original cartoons are now in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

artworks.title: Ancient Pontifical Tapestries
artworks.description: Ancient tapestries from the papal collections, displayed on the right wall.

artworks.title: Bernardino Nocchi Ceiling Frescoes
artworks.description: Ceiling scenes celebrating the virtues of Pius VI foreshadowed in Roman emperors: Nerva, Trajan, Alexander Severus; Clemency of Titus; Antoninus Pius vs. Numa Pompilius.

artworks.title: Trompe-l'oeil Floor Borders
artworks.description: The gallery is famous for its trompe-l'oeil floor borders, creating illusionistic depth patterns in marble.

collections.name: Galleria delle Carte Geografiche
collections.description: A 120-meter long corridor built 1578–1580 by Ottaviano Nonni for Gregory XIII. Frescoed with 40 maps of Italy coordinated by Egnazio Danti. The world's largest pictorial geographical study — the first time Italy was represented as a unified geographical, historical, and cultural entity.

artworks.title: Italia Antiqua and Italia Nova
artworks.description: The two entrance maps of the corridor — ancient Italy and modern Italy — setting the stage for the 32 regional maps that follow.

artworks.title: 32 Regional Maps of Italy
artworks.description: The 32 regional maps of the Italian peninsula arranged north-to-south along the Apennine spine: Piedmont, Liguria, Lombardy, Veneto, Emilia-Romagna, Tuscany, Umbria, Marche, Lazio, Abruzzo, Campania, Puglia, Basilicata, Calabria, Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica, and others.

artworks.title: Maps of Battles and Ports
artworks.description: Eight narrow maps at the ends: Siege of Malta (1565), Battle of Lepanto (1571), Elba, Tremiti Islands; and the four ports: Civitavecchia, Genoa, Venice, Ancona.

artworks.title: 51 Ceiling Panels
artworks.description: 51 panels in rich gilded stucco frames, each depicting a scene from Church history, the Old Testament, or the lives of saints associated with the region below.

collections.name: Stanze di Raffaello (Raphael Rooms)
collections.description: Four rooms in the Apostolic Palace frescoed by Raphael and his workshop for Julius II and Leo X. Together with Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling, they are the grand fresco sequences that mark the High Renaissance in Rome.

artworks.title: The School of Athens
artworks.description: The most famous fresco of the High Renaissance: ancient philosophers gathered in grand imaginary classical architecture. Plato (pointing upward, modeled on Leonardo) and Aristotle (pointing earthward) at the center; Pythagoras, Euclid, Heraclitus (portrait of Michelangelo), Ptolemy, Zoroaster. Raphael painted himself into the group (far right, beside Ptolemy).

artworks.title: The Disputation of the Holy Sacrament
artworks.description: Heaven and earth gather around the Eucharist: the Trinity above, Mary, John the Baptist, martyrs, prophets; below, the Church Militant — saints, doctors, and scholars in animated discussion. A theology of the Eucharist in pictorial form.

artworks.title: The Parnassus
artworks.description: Apollo playing the lyre on Mount Parnassus, surrounded by the nine Muses and poets (Homer, Virgil, Dante, Petrarch) — the domain of poetry and inspiration.

artworks.title: Cardinal and Theological Virtues
artworks.description: Allegorical female figures of Fortitude, Prudence, Temperance (cardinal) and Faith, Hope, Charity (theological), with Justice above.

artworks.title: Ceiling Tondi — Theology, Philosophy, Poetry, Jurisprudence
artworks.description: The four branches of knowledge as personified in medallions, with scenes of Adam and Eve, The Judgment of Solomon, Urania, The Flaying of Marsyas.

artworks.title: The Expulsion of Heliodorus from the Temple
artworks.description: Angels drive the profane Heliodorus from the Temple of Jerusalem, watched from the left by Julius II carried in by Swiss Guard. Dynamic, theatrical composition — a departure from the serene Segnatura style.

artworks.title: The Mass at Bolsena
artworks.description: The 1263 miracle of the bleeding Host at Bolsena, confirming the doctrine of Transubstantiation for a doubting Bohemian priest. Julius II kneels at the altar (lower right).

artworks.title: The Liberation of Saint Peter from Prison
artworks.description: Three scenes in one: the sleeping Peter, the angel freeing him, Peter led past sleeping guards. A study in light: natural moonlight, man-made torchlight, and God-provided angel light.

artworks.title: The Meeting of Pope Leo the Great and Attila
artworks.description: Pope Leo I turns back Attila the Hun in 452, with Sts. Peter and Paul appearing in the sky bearing swords. Portrait of Leo X as the cardinal in the procession.

artworks.title: The Fire in the Borgo
artworks.description: Pope Leo IV extinguishes the 847 fire in the Borgo with the sign of the cross from the Loggia of Blessings. Raphael's design, executed by Giulio Romano.
artworks.location: Stanza dell'Incendio del Borgo, West wall

artworks.title: The Battle of Ostia
artworks.description: Leo IV's naval victory over the Saracens at Ostia, 849.
artworks.location: Stanza dell'Incendio del Borgo, East wall

artworks.title: The Coronation of Charlemagne
artworks.description: Leo III crowns Charlemagne Emperor on Christmas Day, 800 — the foundation of the Holy Roman Empire.
artworks.location: Stanza dell'Incendio del Borgo, South wall

artworks.title: The Oath of Leo III
artworks.description: Leo III purging himself of false accusations before Charlemagne, 800.
artworks.location: Stanza dell'Incendio del Borgo, North wall

artworks.title: The Vision of the Cross
artworks.description: Constantine sees the cross with the sign 'In hoc signo vinces' before the Battle of the Milvian Bridge.

artworks.title: The Battle of the Milvian Bridge
artworks.description: Constantine's victory over Maxentius, 312 CE — the triumph of Christianity over paganism.

artworks.title: The Baptism of Constantine
artworks.description: Constantine baptized by Pope Sylvester I in the Lateran. Sylvester has the features of Pope Clement VII.

artworks.title: The Donation of Constantine
artworks.description: The forged 'Donation' by which Constantine supposedly granted Rome and the West to the Pope — a key text of papal territorial claims.

collections.name: Cappella Sistina (Sistine Chapel)
collections.description: Named for Pope Sixtus IV who restored the Cappella Magna 1477–1480. Consecrated 15 August 1483. The site of the Papal Conclave. Michelangelo's ceiling (1508–1512) and Last Judgment (1536–1541) are the crowning achievements of Western art.

artworks.title: The Creation of Adam
artworks.description: The iconic near-touching hands of God and Adam; Eve watches from beneath God's cloak. Perhaps the most famous image in Western art, painted by Michelangelo as part of the Genesis ceiling cycle.

artworks.title: The Separation of Light from Darkness
artworks.description: God divides light from the void; the final narrative panel painted, with God in dynamic contrapposto.

artworks.title: The Creation of the Sun, Moon and Plants
artworks.description: God creates the luminaries and vegetation, depicted in two movements of the same figure.

artworks.title: The Separation of Land and Water
artworks.description: God divides sea from dry land in a powerful rotational pose.

artworks.title: The Creation of Eve
artworks.description: Eve emerges from Adam's side, hands raised in reverence.

artworks.title: The Fall and Expulsion from the Garden of Eden
artworks.description: Temptation by the serpent and the expulsion combined in one panel — two moments in the same frame.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Noah
artworks.description: Noah offers thanksgiving sacrifice after the Flood.

artworks.title: The Great Flood
artworks.description: Humanity perishes in the Flood; the ark floats in the background. A vortex of drowning figures.

artworks.title: The Drunkenness of Noah
artworks.description: Noah drunk, mocked by his sons — human weakness in the chosen patriarch.

artworks.title: Twelve Prophets and Sibyls
artworks.description: Seated on thrones: Jonah, Jeremiah, Persian Sibyl, Ezekiel, Erythraean Sibyl, Joel, Zechariah, Delphic Sibyl, Isaiah, Cumaean Sibyl, Daniel, Libyan Sibyl.

artworks.title: Four Corner Pendentives
artworks.description: The salvation of Israel: The Brazen Serpent, The Crucifixion of Haman (Esther), David and Goliath, Judith and Holofernes.

artworks.title: Twenty Ignudi
artworks.description: Twenty athletic nude youths framing the five smaller central scenes, each pair enclosing a medallion. Represent the perfection of humanity or angels; a pattern book for later artists.

artworks.title: Ancestors of Christ
artworks.description: 14 lunettes above the windows plus 8 spandrels above them, depicting 40 generations from Abraham to Jesse/David.

artworks.title: The Last Judgment
artworks.description: Christ in glory at the center, surrounded by Mary, apostles, martyrs. The saved rise on the left; the damned are dragged to hell on the right. Charon ferries souls (from Dante); Minos judges. Michelangelo painted his own face onto the flayed skin held by St. Bartholomew.

artworks.title: The Baptism of Christ (North Wall)
artworks.description: Christ baptized by John in the Jordan — the first fresco on the north wall (Life of Christ cycle).

artworks.title: The Trials of Moses (South Wall)
artworks.description: Botticelli's masterpiece in the chapel: the killing of the Egyptian, defending Jethro's daughters, the Burning Bush.

artworks.title: The Temptations of Christ (North Wall)
artworks.description: Christ tested by the devil; temple pinnacle scene.

artworks.title: The Calling of Peter and Andrew (North Wall)
artworks.description: Christ calls the first apostles by the Sea of Galilee.

artworks.title: The Handing over of the Keys (North Wall)
artworks.description: 'You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church' — Christ gives the keys to Peter.

artworks.title: The Crossing of the Red Sea (South Wall)
artworks.description: Israel escapes Egypt; Pharaoh's army overwhelmed by the waters.

artworks.title: The Handing over of the Tablets of the Law (South Wall)
artworks.description: Sinai, golden calf worship, punishment, return of the Tablets.

artworks.title: The Punishment of Korah, Dathan and Abiram (South Wall)
artworks.description: The rebel priests swallowed by the earth — a dramatic composition of divine punishment.

artworks.title: The Testament and Death of Moses (South Wall)
artworks.description: Moses' final address and death on Mount Nebo — powerful figures in dramatic landscape.

artworks.title: The Sermon on the Mount (North Wall)
artworks.description: Christ delivers the Beatitudes to the crowds.

artworks.title: The Journey of Moses in Egypt (South Wall)
artworks.description: Combines farewell to Jethro, return to Egypt, circumcision of Moses' son.

artworks.title: Marble Transenna (Choir Screen)
artworks.artist: Mino da Fiesole, Andrea Bregno, Giovanni Dalmata
artworks.description: The marble screen dividing the chapel into sanctuary and nave, surmounted by ornate candlesticks and the papal coat of arms of Sixtus IV.

artworks.title: Raphael Tapestries (Sistine Chapel)
artworks.medium: Wool, silk, gold and silver thread
artworks.description: Ten tapestries depicting events from the Lives of St. Peter and St. Paul, commissioned by Leo X. Looted during the Sack of Rome (1527); a set reassembled and displayed again from 1983.

collections.name: Pinacoteca Vaticana
collections.description: Inaugurated 27 October 1932 in a building purpose-built by architect Luca Beltrami for Pius XI. Approximately 460 paintings in 18 chronological rooms, from the 'Primitives' (12th–13th c.) to the 19th century.

artworks.title: Stefaneschi Triptych
artworks.medium: Tempera on wood, central panel 178 x 89 cm
artworks.description: Commissioned by Cardinal Jacopo Stefaneschi for Old St. Peter's. Painted on both sides: front — Christ enthroned with the Crucifixion of St. Peter and Martyrdom of St. Paul; back — St. Peter enthroned holding the model of the triptych. A supreme Giotto work.

artworks.title: Stories of St. Nicholas of Bari
artworks.description: Fra Angelico's luminous devotional panels depicting the life of St. Nicholas — golden, radiant, and deeply spiritual.

artworks.title: Sixtus IV appoints Bartolomeo Platina Prefect of the Vatican Library
artworks.description: The great fresco from the Vatican Library — portrait group including Cardinal Giuliano della Rovere (future Julius II). A masterpiece of Quattrocento perspective and portraiture.

artworks.title: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints Dominic and Catherine
artworks.description: A serene devotional panel showing the Madonna enthroned with Saints Dominic and Catherine of Siena.

artworks.title: The Transfiguration
artworks.description: Raphael's final masterpiece: two scenes in one canvas — Christ blazing on Mount Tabor above, the apostles failing to heal the possessed boy below. Left unfinished at his death (1520). Arguably the most influential altarpiece of the High Renaissance.

artworks.title: Madonna of Foligno
artworks.medium: Oil on canvas transferred from wood
artworks.description: The Madonna and Child with saints and a kneeling donor (Sigismondo de' Conti), set against the town of Foligno. Painted for the high altar of Santa Maria in Aracoeli.

artworks.title: The Coronation of the Virgin
artworks.medium: Oil on canvas transferred from wood
artworks.description: Christ crowns the Virgin Mary in a celestial mandorla, surrounded by angels — an early Raphael masterpiece from his Florentine period.

artworks.title: St. Jerome in the Wilderness
artworks.description: The only Leonardo in Rome — an unfinished panel revealing his working method. A gaunt, kneeling Jerome beating his chest with a stone, lion at his feet, underdrawing visible.

artworks.title: Lamentation over the Dead Christ
artworks.description: Venetian colorism in a Pietà — the cimasa of the Pesaro Altarpiece, showing Christ's body mourned by the Virgin and St. John.

artworks.title: Creator on the Rainbow amid Angels
artworks.description: God the Father on a rainbow amid angels — from the Triptych of Humanity, showing Correggio's early mastery of soft color and light.

artworks.title: Madonna and Child in Glory with Saints
artworks.description: Venetian colorism at its summit — a vibrant altarpiece with the Madonna in glory above and saints below.

artworks.title: The Madonna of the Cherries
artworks.description: Late Renaissance tenderness and chromatic warmth — the Madonna offers cherries to the Christ Child.

artworks.title: The Deposition (Entombment of Christ)
artworks.description: Christ lowered onto a marble slab that juts into the viewer's space; harsh light, straining hands, the diagonal uniting altar and tomb. Defined Baroque naturalism. Commissioned for the church of Santa Maria in Vallicella.

artworks.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Erasmus
artworks.description: The brutal martyrdom of St. Erasmus, wound on a windlass — Poussin's classical French Baroque at its most disciplined and dramatic.

artworks.title: The Last Communion of Saint Jerome
artworks.description: St. Jerome receiving the Eucharist on his deathbed — a Baroque masterpiece of devotional intensity and dramatic lighting.

artworks.title: Models for St. Peter's Chair (Cathedra Petri)
artworks.description: Terracotta models and bozzetti for Bernini's great bronze Cathedra Petri in the apse of St. Peter's Basilica — showing his creative process.

artworks.title: Portrait of George IV of England
artworks.description: Elegant Regency state portrait of George IV, showing Lawrence's mastery of aristocratic portraiture.

artworks.title: Crucifixion of Saint Peter
artworks.description: St. Peter crucified upside down — Reni's classical Baroque composition of dramatic simplicity.

artworks.title: Saint Matthew and the Angel
artworks.description: The evangelist Matthew with his angel — a Reni masterpiece combining grace and Baroque dynamism.

collections.name: Appartamento Borgia (Borgia Apartment)
collections.description: Pope Alexander VI (Rodrigo Borgia) commissioned Pinturicchio to decorate his private apartments 1492–1494. Six monumental rooms with lavish stucco, gilded panels, and esoteric iconography. Now houses the Collection of Modern and Contemporary Art.

artworks.title: Room of the Liberal Arts
artworks.description: Grammar, Rhetoric, Logic (Trivium); Geometry, Arithmetic, Music, Astronomy (Quadrivium) — celestial women personifying the liberal arts with their patrons. Ceiling with Borgia heraldry (bull, double crown).

artworks.title: Room of the Saints
artworks.description: St. Elizabeth, St. Anthony Abbot & St. Paul the Hermit, St. Catherine's Disputation, St. Barbara, St. Susanna, St. Sebastian; ceiling with the Isis-Osiris myth. Recognized as a Pinturicchio masterpiece; tondo of the Madonna and Child said to portray Giulia Farnese.

artworks.title: Room of the Mysteries
artworks.description: Annunciation, Nativity, Adoration of the Magi, Resurrection, Ascension, Pentecost, Assumption. Alexander VI kneels at Christ's feet in the Resurrection. Believed to be the earliest European depiction of Native Americans.

artworks.title: Room of the Sibyls
artworks.description: Twelve sibyls paired with Old Testament prophets on deep blue ground; scrolls foretelling Christ; astrological/planetary program.

artworks.title: Room of the Creed
artworks.description: The 12 Apostles paired with Old Testament prophets, reciting the verses of the Apostle's Creed on scrolls — a bridge between Old and New Testament material.

artworks.title: Room of the Pontiffs
artworks.description: Papal portraits in lunettes — the oldest wing, with portraits from Nicholas III onward.

collections.name: Collezione d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea
collections.description: Inaugurated 23 June 1973 by Paul VI, following his 1964 address calling for renewed dialogue between the Church and contemporary art. Approximately 8,000 works by 250 artists in 55 rooms along the Borgia Apartment.

artworks.title: Pietà (after Delacroix)
artworks.description: Painted months before his suicide; the lifeless Christ possibly a self-portrait. Van Gogh's masterpiece in the Vatican — one of his last works.

artworks.title: Le Christ et le peintre
artworks.description: Chagall's dreamlike iconographic universe applied to religious subjects — Christ as painter, a self-referential meditation on art and faith.

artworks.title: Matisse Room — Vence Chapel Preparatory Drawings
artworks.description: Full-scale preparatory drawings (over 5 meters high) for the Vence Chapel stained glass, plus drawing of the Virgin and Child, bronze altar cross, silk chasubles. The complete creative genesis of Matisse's only religious building. Donated by his son Pierre in 1980.

artworks.title: Study for Velazquez Pope II
artworks.description: After Velazquez's Portrait of Innocent X — Bacon's screaming pope, one of the most powerful images of existential anguish in modern art.

artworks.title: L'Annuncio
artworks.description: Surrealist Annunciation — Dali's distinctive blend of religious iconography and dream imagery.

artworks.title: Le figlie di Loth III
artworks.description: The daughters of Lot — Carrà's Metaphysical treatment of the biblical subject.

artworks.title: Aetas Aurea
artworks.description: Delicate wax sculpture by the Italian Impressionist sculptor, capturing light and form in a unique medium.

artworks.title: Wooden Bas-relief (from Tahiti)
artworks.description: Rare sculptural work probably from Gauguin's first Tahiti stay — the artist's Polynesian influence translated into wood.

artworks.title: Cavaliere
artworks.description: The horse and rider theme — Marini's iconic modern sculpture of the equestrian figure.

artworks.title: Catrame II
artworks.description: Part of Burri's revolutionary 'Catrame' (tar) series — using industrial materials to create abstract surfaces of profound depth.

artworks.title: Christ and the Fisherman
artworks.description: Another Chagall religious work showing Christ with a fisherman, blending the sacred and the everyday.

collections.name: Sfera con Sfera (Sphere Within Sphere)
collections.description: Arnaldo Pomodoro's masterpiece in the Cortile della Pigna — a large sphere fissured to reveal a complex inner world. Donated by the artist in 1990.

artworks.title: Sfera con Sfera
artworks.medium: Polished bronze, diameter 4 m, weight ~4 tons
artworks.description: A large sphere fissured to reveal a complex inner world of gears and mechanical forms; can rotate on a ball-bearing mechanism. Metaphor: the tension between exterior perfection and interior complexity; 'spirit and matter'; a 'wounded planet.' Sister spheres exist worldwide (UN Headquarters, Trinity College Dublin).

collections.name: Bramante (Momo) Staircase
collections.description: Giuseppe Momo's 1932 double-helix spiral staircase — the exit route for all visitors. Two separate ramps so ascending and descending visitors never cross.

artworks.title: Bramante Staircase (Double Helix)
artworks.description: A double helix — two separate ramps so ascending and descending visitors never cross. Encircles a ~15 meter diameter stairwell with a clear central void. Shallow incline (stepped ramp, not a true staircase); ornately worked metal balustrade. All visitors exit via this route. Often compared to Frank Lloyd Wright's Guggenheim (20 years earlier).

artworks.title: Original Bramante Staircase
artworks.description: The original double spiral in a square tower by Donato Bramante, inside the Pio-Clementino Museum.

collections.name: Cappella Niccolina (Niccoline Chapel)
collections.description: Fra Angelico's fresco cycle (1447–1449) for Pope Nicholas V — the earliest complete fresco cycle in the Vatican, predating the Sistine Chapel by decades.

artworks.title: Scenes from the Life of St. Stephen
artworks.description: The chapel's fresco cycle depicts the life of the first Christian martyr, St. Stephen, with luminous colors and delicate compositions.

artworks.title: Scenes from the Life of St. Lawrence
artworks.description: The life of St. Lawrence, deacon and martyr, depicted with Fra Angelico's characteristic grace and luminous color.
